turns:
This repo has no .gitignore. Add one covering the usual Python build and cache artifacts.

Rules relevant to this task:
- Before your first write, create a branch for the task and do the work there. Never commit to the default branch. Branch names follow type/kebab-description, where type is one of feature, bugfix, hotfix, chore, release, docs.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): subject, where type is one of feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, ci, build, perf, style.

events.command:
git add .gitignore && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
chore(repo): add Python .gitignore

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git status --short

events.text:
Added `.gitignore` on branch `chore/add-python-gitignore`, committed as `12b53b1`.

Coverage: bytecode/`__pycache__`, C extensions, packaging & dist artifacts, test/coverage output, type-checker and linter caches (mypy, pyre, pytype, ruff), virtualenvs and `.env`, Jupyter checkpoints, Sphinx build, and `__pypackages__`.

One thing to note: I included `lib/` and `var/` since they're in the standard Python template, but they're generic enough that they'd shadow a real source directory by that name. Nothing in the repo conflicts today (only three top-level `.py` files), so I left them in — say the word if you'd rather drop them.
